subject: SCI
title: Science 5
description: Fifth-grade NGSS science organized around the CA Science Framework's grade 5 storyline: matter is made of tiny particles that are conserved through change, plants build their bodies from air and water using the sun's energy, matter and energy cycle through ecosystems, Earth's four spheres interact, water is unevenly distributed, communities protect resources, and patterns of shadows and stars come from Earth's motion in space. Nearly every week includes a hands-on investigation with household materials, a science notebook entry, and a claim-evidence-reasoning (CER) write-up. Engineering design challenges are woven in and featured in two dedicated units.
framework: California Next Generation Science Standards (CA NGSS); 2016 California Science Framework

standards.5-PS1-1: Develop a model to describe that matter is made of particles too small to be seen.
standards.5-PS1-2: Measure and graph quantities to provide evidence that the total weight of matter is conserved when heating, cooling, or mixing substances.
standards.5-PS1-3: Make observations and measurements to identify materials based on their properties.
standards.5-PS1-4: Conduct an investigation to determine whether the mixing of two or more substances results in new substances.
standards.5-PS2-1: Support an argument that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed down.
standards.5-PS3-1: Use models to describe that energy in animals' food (used for repair, growth, motion, and warmth) was once energy from the sun.
standards.5-LS1-1: Support an argument that plants get the materials they need for growth chiefly from air and water.
standards.5-LS2-1: Develop a model to describe the movement of matter among plants, animals, decomposers, and the environment.
standards.5-ESS1-1: Support an argument that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars are due to their relative distances from Earth.
standards.5-ESS1-2: Represent data in graphical displays to reveal patterns of daily changes in shadows, day and night, and the seasonal appearance of some stars.
standards.5-ESS2-1: Develop a model using an example to describe ways the geosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere, and/or atmosphere interact.
standards.5-ESS2-2: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
standards.5-ESS3-1: Obtain and combine information about ways individual communities use science ideas to protect the Earth's resources and environment.
standards.3-5-ETS1-1: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost.
standards.3-5-ETS1-2: Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints.
standards.3-5-ETS1-3: Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.

units.title: Matter Is Made of Particles
units.big_idea: All matter is made of particles too small to see, and materials can be identified by their properties.

units.title: Changes in Matter
units.big_idea: When substances change or mix, weight is conserved, and sometimes new substances form.

units.title: Engineering Design: Water Filter Challenge
units.big_idea: Engineers define problems, compare solutions and use fair tests to improve designs.

units.title: Plants, Food and Energy from the Sun
units.big_idea: Plants build their bodies mostly from air and water, capturing the sun's energy that animals later use.

units.title: Ecosystems: Cycling Matter
units.big_idea: Matter moves among producers, consumers, decomposers and the environment in a continuous cycle.

units.title: Earth's Interacting Systems
units.big_idea: The geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere constantly interact to shape Earth.

units.title: Water on Earth
units.big_idea: Most of Earth's water is salty or frozen, so fresh water is precious.

units.title: Protecting Earth's Resources
units.big_idea: Communities use science to reduce human impact on land, water, air and living things.

units.title: Gravity and the Stars
units.big_idea: Earth's gravity pulls everything toward its center, and stars look bright or dim depending on distance.

units.title: Patterns in the Sky
units.big_idea: Earth's rotation and orbit cause daily shadow patterns, day and night, and seasonal star patterns.

units.title: Capstone Investigation
units.big_idea: Scientists ask questions, plan investigations, analyze data and communicate findings.

weeks.topic: The mystery of disappearing sugar: evidence for particles
objectives: Observe that dissolved matter is still present
Draw a first particle model

days.title: Where did it go?
days.work: Stir a spoonful of sugar into warm water, observe it 'disappear,' then taste a drop and record observations and questions in a science notebook.

days.title: Weighing the evidence
days.work: Weigh water and sugar separately, mix them, and weigh again; record data in a table and discuss what it shows.

days.title: Evaporation clue
days.work: Put a few drops of the sugar water on a dark plate in a sunny window to evaporate and predict what will be left.

days.title: Modeling particles
days.work: Check the evaporated plate for sugar crystals and draw a particle model of sugar dissolving in water, before and after.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning (CER) paragraph answering 'Is the sugar still there?' using weight and evaporation data.

weeks.assessment: CER paragraph and particle model drawing.

objectives: Gather evidence that air has weight and takes up space
Model gas particles

days.title: Air takes up space
days.work: Push an upside-down cup with a paper towel inside into a bowl of water and explain why the towel stays dry.

days.title: Air has weight
days.work: Build a balance from a ruler and two balloons, then pop one and observe the balance tip; record findings.

days.title: Compressing air
days.work: Pump air into a deflated ball and weigh it before and after; compress air in a capped syringe and describe the particles.

days.title: Particle simulation
days.work: Use the PhET 'States of Matter: Basics' simulation to compare particle motion in solids, liquids and gases and sketch each.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise last week's particle model to include gases and explain how particles too small to see can still have weight.

weeks.assessment: Revised particle model with written explanation; investigation data tables.

objectives: Measure and describe physical properties
Use properties to identify materials
materials: samples: aluminum foil, paper clip, plastic spoon, wooden stick, rubber band, glass marble, salt, baking soda
battery, bulb and wires (simple circuit kit)

days.title: Describing properties
days.work: Observe 8 material samples and record color, texture, hardness (scratch test) and flexibility in a table.

days.title: Magnetism and reflectivity
days.work: Test each sample with a magnet and a flashlight beam and add results to the table.

days.title: Electrical conductivity
days.work: Build a simple circuit with a battery and bulb and test which samples complete the circuit.

days.title: Thermal conductivity
days.work: Place metal, plastic and wooden spoons in hot water and compare which handle warms fastest after 3 minutes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Use the property table to identify 3 'mystery' materials and explain which properties gave them away.

weeks.assessment: Property data table and mystery-material identification with explanations.

objectives: Plan tests to identify white powders
Use solubility and reactions as properties
materials: iodine or tincture (adult supervised) or red cabbage juice

days.title: Observing powders
days.work: Examine 5 known white powders with a magnifying glass and record texture, crystal shape and feel.

days.title: Water test
days.work: Add each powder to water and record whether it dissolves, clumps or settles.

days.title: Vinegar and indicator tests
days.work: Test each powder with vinegar (fizzing) and an indicator (adult-supervised iodine or cabbage juice) and record results.

days.title: Mystery mixture
days.work: Identify an adult-prepared mystery powder (or mixture of two) using the test results chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER identifying the mystery powder and take a quiz on material properties.

weeks.assessment: Powder test chart, CER and properties quiz.

weeks.topic: Particle model and states of matter
objectives: Explain melting, freezing and evaporation with particle models
Communicate a model of matter

days.title: Melting race
days.work: Time ice cubes melting in different places (hand, counter, sunny window) and graph the times.

days.title: Food coloring diffusion
days.work: Drop food coloring into hot and cold water and compare how quickly it spreads, linking speed to particle motion.

days.title: Evaporation and condensation
days.work: Observe water boiling and condensing on a cold lid (adult handles the stove) and draw particle diagrams for each step.

days.title: Model poster
days.work: Create a poster showing particle arrangements in solid, liquid and gas with arrows for melting, freezing, evaporating and condensing.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Take a Unit 1 assessment on particles and properties and present the model poster.

weeks.assessment: Unit 1 test and particle model poster rubric.

weeks.topic: Conservation of weight when melting and freezing
objectives: Measure weight before and after a change of state
Graph data as evidence of conservation

days.title: Prediction
days.work: Predict whether a sealed bag of ice will weigh more, less or the same after melting, and explain the prediction.

days.title: Melting test
days.work: Weigh 3 sealed bags of ice, let them melt and reweigh, recording data in a table.

days.title: Freezing test
days.work: Weigh sealed bags of water, freeze overnight and reweigh; also melt chocolate chips in a sealed bag in warm water and reweigh.

days.title: Graphing
days.work: Create a bar graph comparing before and after weights for all trials and calculate any differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER on whether weight is conserved during melting and freezing, explaining small measurement errors.

weeks.assessment: Bar graph and CER on conservation.

objectives: Distinguish mixtures from solutions
Separate mixtures by their properties

days.title: Making mixtures
days.work: Make a trail-mix and a sand-and-salt mixture, weigh each part and the whole, and record whether weight adds up.

days.title: Separation plan
days.work: Plan how to separate sand, salt, paper clips and rice using properties (magnetism, size, solubility).

days.title: Separating
days.work: Carry out the separation plan with a magnet, sieve, water and coffee filter, then set salt water to evaporate.

days.title: Recovering the salt
days.work: Weigh the recovered salt and compare with the starting amount; explain any differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a procedure for separating a new mixture and take a quiz on mixtures vs. solutions.

weeks.assessment: Separation procedure and data; mixtures quiz.

objectives: Identify evidence of a new substance
Test whether mixing produces new substances

days.title: Signs of reaction
days.work: Learn the signs of a new substance (gas, color change, temperature change, new solid) and mix baking soda and vinegar, recording observations.

days.title: Milk and lemon
days.work: Add lemon juice to warm milk and observe curds forming; compare to milk mixed with water.

days.title: Rust investigation
days.work: Set up steel wool samples (dry, wet, wet with vinegar) in jars to observe rusting over the week.

days.title: Cabbage indicator
days.work: Make red cabbage juice indicator and test 6 household liquids, recording color changes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Sort 10 changes as making new substances or not, using evidence from the investigations, and check the rust jars.

weeks.assessment: Observation tables and change sorting with evidence.

objectives: Measure weight in open and closed reactions
Explain conservation using a particle model

days.title: Open reaction
days.work: Weigh vinegar and baking soda in an open cup before and after reacting and record the weight change.

days.title: Closed reaction
days.work: Repeat the reaction in a bottle sealed with a balloon and compare the before and after weights.

days.title: Explaining the difference
days.work: Graph both trials and explain why weight seemed to decrease in the open cup using particles of gas escaping.

days.title: Rust results
days.work: Examine the rust jars, describe evidence of a new substance, and connect the result to particles rearranging.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 2 assessment on conservation and new substances and write a final CER.

weeks.assessment: Unit 2 test; CER on conservation in chemical reactions.

weeks.topic: Designing a water filter: define and generate
objectives: Define criteria and constraints for a design problem
Generate and compare multiple solutions

days.title: The problem
days.work: Read about communities without clean water and define the design problem with criteria (clearest water) and constraints (materials, budget of play money).

days.title: Testing materials
days.work: Test each filter material alone and record how clear the dirty water becomes on a 1–5 turbidity scale.

days.title: Brainstorming designs
days.work: Sketch 3 different filter designs with labeled layers and estimated cost.

days.title: Choosing a design
days.work: Compare the 3 designs in a decision matrix against criteria and constraints and choose one to build.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Build the first prototype and write a prediction of how it will perform.

weeks.assessment: Design notebook: criteria/constraints, sketches and decision matrix.

objectives: Plan and carry out fair tests
Identify failure points and improve a prototype

days.title: Fair test
days.work: Run the same amount of dirty water through the prototype, measuring clarity, time and volume recovered.

days.title: Failure points
days.work: Identify where the filter failed (leaks, cloudy water, slow flow) and plan one change.

days.title: Redesign
days.work: Build version 2 changing only one variable and test it under the same conditions.

days.title: Comparing results
days.work: Graph results of both versions and discuss why filtered water is still not safe to drink without disinfection.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the final filter design and write a reflection on how fair tests guided improvements.

weeks.assessment: Engineering presentation and data comparison graph.

weeks.topic: Where does a plant's mass come from?
objectives: Investigate whether plants get mass from soil
Analyze historical evidence (van Helmont's willow)

days.title: Initial ideas
days.work: Write and draw initial ideas about where a giant tree's material comes from.

days.title: Van Helmont's experiment
days.work: Read about Jan van Helmont's 5-year willow experiment and analyze his data on tree mass and soil mass.

days.title: Set up investigation
days.work: Weigh dry soil and plant bean seeds in cups, recording starting soil mass for a multi-week investigation.

days.title: Hydroponic test
days.work: Start seeds on wet paper towels in a bag with no soil to see if plants can grow without soil.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a preliminary claim about where plant mass comes from, citing van Helmont's evidence.

weeks.assessment: Initial model and preliminary claim; investigation setup check.

objectives: Gather evidence that plants use carbon dioxide and water
Explain the role of light

days.title: Floating leaf disks
days.work: Do the floating leaf disk investigation with spinach in baking soda water under a lamp and count disks rising over time.

days.title: Light vs. dark
days.work: Repeat the leaf disk test in darkness and compare results to show plants need light.

days.title: Stomata peel
days.work: Paint clear nail polish on a leaf, peel it with tape, and look for stomata with a magnifier or phone microscope.

days.title: Plant growth check
days.work: Measure plant heights in the soil cups and paper towel bags and record growth data.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a model showing air and water entering a plant and sugar being made, then take a quiz.

weeks.assessment: Leaf disk data and plant model diagram; quiz.

weeks.topic: Energy in food comes from the sun
objectives: Trace energy from the sun to food to animals
Describe how animals use food energy

days.title: Tracing breakfast
days.work: Trace every food in your breakfast back to a plant and the sun with arrows.

days.title: How bodies use energy
days.work: Measure your pulse and body temperature at rest and after exercise and discuss how food energy powers motion and warmth.

days.title: Food labels
days.work: Compare calories on 5 food labels and explain that calories measure stored energy originally from sunlight.

days.title: Energy model
days.work: Create an energy flow diagram from sun to grass to cow to human, labeling uses of energy at each step.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation of how the energy used to run a race was once energy from the sun.

weeks.assessment: Energy flow diagram and written explanation.

objectives: Analyze soil mass data from the plant investigation
Argue that plants gain mass chiefly from air and water

days.title: Harvest
days.work: Carefully remove plants, dry the soil and weigh it; compare to starting soil mass.

days.title: Plant mass
days.work: Weigh the plants and compare the gain in plant mass to the change in soil mass in a table.

days.title: Graphing
days.work: Graph soil mass change vs. plant mass gain for each cup.

days.title: Argument writing
days.work: Write a scientific argument with claim, evidence from your data and van Helmont, and reasoning about air and water.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 4 assessment and share the argument aloud with family.

weeks.assessment: Written scientific argument; Unit 4 test.

weeks.topic: Food webs: producers, consumers and decomposers
objectives: Identify roles of organisms in an ecosystem
Build a food web model
materials: photos of a CA ecosystem (chaparral or kelp forest)

days.title: Roles in ecosystems
days.work: Sort 20 organism cards from a California kelp forest into producers, consumers and decomposers.

days.title: Food chains
days.work: Build 4 food chains from the cards with arrows showing the direction of matter and energy.

days.title: Food web
days.work: Connect the chains with yarn into a food web and identify organisms that connect to many others.

days.title: What if?
days.work: Remove sea otters from the web and predict the effects on urchins and kelp; read about the real kelp forest decline.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a labeled food web for a local backyard ecosystem and take a vocabulary quiz.

weeks.assessment: Backyard food web; vocabulary quiz.

objectives: Observe decomposition
Explain how decomposers return matter to soil and air

days.title: Mold investigation
days.work: Set up sealed bags with bread under different conditions (dry, damp, fridge, warm) to observe mold growth (do not open).

days.title: Bottle compost
days.work: Build a mini compost column in a clear bottle with soil, leaves and fruit scraps and draw day 1.

days.title: Decomposer research
days.work: Read about fungi, bacteria and worms and explain how each breaks down dead matter.

days.title: Observations
days.work: Record and sketch changes in the mold bags and compost column with dates.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Add decomposers to last week's food web with arrows back to soil and air and explain the cycle.

weeks.assessment: Observation log and revised food web with decomposers.

weeks.topic: Modeling matter cycling in an ecosystem
objectives: Build a closed terrarium
Model movement of matter among organisms and the environment

days.title: Build a terrarium
days.work: Build a closed terrarium with gravel, soil, plants and (optionally) pill bugs, and diagram its parts.

days.title: Predicting cycles
days.work: Predict how water, oxygen, carbon dioxide and nutrients will move in the sealed jar.

days.title: Observing
days.work: Observe condensation on the jar walls and plant health and record observations.

days.title: Mold and compost update
days.work: Record final observations of mold bags and compost column and compare to day 1.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a matter-cycle model of the terrarium showing arrows for water, gases and nutrients.

weeks.assessment: Terrarium matter-cycle model.

objectives: Explain how changes affect an ecosystem
Argue using evidence about ecosystem health
materials: articles on California invasive species (e.g., quagga mussels, Argentine ants)

days.title: Invasive species
days.work: Read about an invasive species in California and diagram how it disrupts the food web.

days.title: Population data
days.work: Graph sample population data for predators and prey over 10 years and describe the pattern.

days.title: Ecosystem game
days.work: Play an 'Oh Deer' style game with family modeling food, water and shelter and record population changes each round.

days.title: Terrarium update
days.work: Observe the terrarium and explain whether matter is cycling successfully.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 5 assessment on food webs, decomposers and matter cycling.

weeks.assessment: Population graph; Unit 5 test.

objectives: Define the geosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere
Find sphere interactions in a local place

days.title: Four spheres
days.work: Watch a NASA Space Place video on Earth's systems and create a four-quadrant chart with examples of each sphere.

days.title: Outdoor survey
days.work: Survey a yard or park and list 10 things you observe, labeling each with its sphere.

days.title: Finding interactions
days.work: Identify 5 interactions from the survey (rain soaking soil, roots breaking rock) and draw arrows between spheres.

days.title: Satellite views
days.work: Examine NASA satellite images of a hurricane and a wildfire and identify which spheres are interacting.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take a spheres quiz and explain one interaction in a paragraph.

weeks.assessment: Sphere interaction chart and quiz.

objectives: Model how water and wind shape land
Explain geosphere-hydrosphere interactions

days.title: Shake test
days.work: Shake sugar cubes or small rocks in a jar with water for 3 minutes and observe physical weathering.

days.title: Stream table
days.work: Build a sloped sand-and-soil pan and pour water slowly to observe erosion and deposition; sketch the channel and delta.

days.title: Variables
days.work: Repeat the stream table test with a steeper slope and with plants (grass clumps) and compare erosion.

days.title: Wind erosion
days.work: Use a hair dryer on dry sand to model wind erosion and compare to wet sand.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about how the sphere interactions changed the land in the models and connect to a CA example (Yosemite Valley or coastal cliffs).

weeks.assessment: Stream table sketches and written explanation.

objectives: Model how the atmosphere and hydrosphere interact in weather
Explain how ocean temperatures affect climate

days.title: Cloud in a jar
days.work: Make a cloud in a jar with hot water and ice and explain the role of water vapor and cooling.

days.title: Ocean currents
days.work: Model warm and cold water currents with colored hot and cold water in a clear container and observe.

days.title: Weather tracking
days.work: Record temperature, cloud cover and precipitation daily for the week in a weather log.

days.title: Coastal climate
days.work: Compare average temperatures of San Francisco and Sacramento and explain how the ocean affects climate.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Draw a model showing how the atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere interact during a rainstorm.

weeks.assessment: Rainstorm sphere-interaction model; weather log.

weeks.topic: Sphere interactions in a California event
objectives: Develop a model of sphere interactions in a real event
Communicate the model to others
materials: articles on California wildfires and mudslides

days.title: Case study
days.work: Read about a California wildfire followed by winter mudslides and list each sphere involved.

days.title: Cause-effect chain
days.work: Build a cause-and-effect chain showing how the fire changed the biosphere and how rain then affected the geosphere.

days.title: Model poster
days.work: Create a poster model of the event with arrows labeling each sphere interaction.

days.title: Presentation
days.work: Present the model to family and answer questions about how humans are part of the biosphere.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 6 assessment on Earth's spheres and their interactions.

weeks.assessment: Model poster rubric and Unit 6 test.

objectives: Describe the amounts of water in Earth's reservoirs
Graph the percentages of salt water and fresh water

days.title: Model all the water
days.work: Use 1 liter of water to model Earth's water, measuring out 97% ocean, then dividing the remaining 3% into ice, groundwater and surface water.

days.title: USGS data
days.work: Read USGS Water Science School data on water distribution and record percentages in a table.

days.title: Graphing
days.work: Make a circle graph and a bar graph of salt water vs. fresh water and fresh-water reservoirs.

days.title: Thinking about the data
days.work: Answer questions like 'What fraction of fresh water is easily available?' using the graphs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an explanation, using the graphs as evidence, for why fresh water is a limited resource.

weeks.assessment: Graphs and written explanation.

weeks.topic: California's water: sources and the water cycle
objectives: Trace where California's water comes from
Model the water cycle connecting reservoirs

days.title: Water cycle in a bag
days.work: Draw the water cycle on a zip bag with a little water, tape it to a sunny window, and observe evaporation and condensation.

days.title: California snowpack
days.work: Read about the Sierra Nevada snowpack and trace on a map how it reaches cities through rivers and aqueducts.

days.title: Groundwater
days.work: Build an aquifer model in a clear cup with gravel, sand and clay and pour 'rain' to show how groundwater forms.

days.title: Home water audit
days.work: Measure how much water your family uses in one day by estimating faucet, shower and toilet use.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 7 assessment on water distribution and graph reading.

weeks.assessment: Home water audit; Unit 7 test.

weeks.topic: Human impact on land, water and air
objectives: Identify ways human activities affect Earth's systems
Obtain information from multiple sources
materials: articles from NASA Climate Kids and EPA kids pages

days.title: Resources
days.work: Sort 15 resources as renewable or nonrenewable and discuss how each is used in your home.

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Coat index cards with petroleum jelly, place them indoors and outdoors, and check particulates at week's end.

days.title: Trash audit
days.work: Weigh and sort one day of household trash into recycling, compost, landfill and hazardous categories.

days.title: Reading about impacts
days.work: Read two articles about human impacts (plastic in oceans, groundwater overuse) and take notes.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Examine the particulate cards with a magnifier and write a summary of human impacts on two spheres.

weeks.assessment: Trash audit data and impact summary.

objectives: Research how communities use science to protect resources
Combine information from multiple sources
materials: articles on California efforts (e.g., Monterey Bay sanctuary, water-wise landscaping, condor recovery)

days.title: Case studies
days.work: Read about two California conservation projects and record the problem, science used and results.

days.title: Local research
days.work: Find what your city does with recycling, stormwater and water conservation using its website.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Interview a family member or neighbor about one way they conserve resources and record their answers.

days.title: Combining information
days.work: Combine notes from 3 sources into a one-page fact sheet on protecting a resource.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Share the fact sheet and take a quiz on conservation strategies.

weeks.assessment: Fact sheet from multiple sources; quiz.

weeks.topic: Engineering a solution: reduce, reuse or protect
objectives: Design a solution to an environmental problem
Test and improve a prototype

days.title: Define the problem
days.work: Choose a problem (oil spill cleanup or water-saving planter) and define criteria and constraints.

days.title: Design options
days.work: Sketch two possible solutions and compare their trade-offs.

days.title: Build and test
days.work: Build a prototype from recycled materials and test it (e.g., cleaning a vegetable-oil spill from water with cotton, feathers, sponge).

days.title: Improve
days.work: Identify a failure point, change one variable, and retest.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Present the solution and take the Unit 8 assessment on protecting Earth's resources.

weeks.assessment: Engineering notebook and presentation; Unit 8 test.

weeks.topic: Gravity pulls down toward Earth's center
objectives: Gather evidence that gravity acts downward everywhere on Earth
Model gravity on a round Earth

days.title: Drop tests
days.work: Drop balls of different masses from the same height and record which lands first.

days.title: Plumb line
days.work: Make a plumb line and test whether it always points the same direction in different places.

days.title: Round Earth
days.work: Place figurines around a globe and draw arrows showing 'down' for people in California, Australia and Antarctica.

days.title: Gravity simulation
days.work: Explore the PhET 'Gravity and Orbits' simulation and record how gravity affects motion.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an argument that gravity on Earth is directed toward its center using evidence from the investigations.

weeks.assessment: Written argument about gravity's direction.

objectives: Compare the sun to other stars
Investigate how distance affects apparent brightness

days.title: Sun as a star
days.work: Read NASA Space Place 'What is a Star?' and compare the sun to other stars in a chart.

days.title: Flashlight investigation
days.work: In a dark room, compare the brightness of identical flashlights at 1 m, 3 m and 6 m and record observations.

days.title: Measuring brightness
days.work: Use a light meter app or a paper-layer test to measure brightness at different distances and graph the data.

days.title: Star distances
days.work: Compare the distances of the sun, Sirius and Betelgeuse with a scale model using a long hallway or sidewalk.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER explaining why the sun looks brighter than other stars.

weeks.assessment: Brightness graph and CER.

weeks.topic: Scale of the solar system and stars
objectives: Build a scale model of distances
Argue about brightness and distance with data
materials: toilet paper roll or measuring tape

days.title: Toilet paper solar system
days.work: Build a toilet-paper scale model of planet distances from the sun along a hallway.

days.title: Size model
days.work: Compare the sizes of the sun and planets with balls and seeds and discuss scale.

days.title: Gravity and orbits
days.work: Swing a ball on a string to model how gravity keeps planets in orbit and explain what happens if the string is cut.

days.title: Brightness data
days.work: Analyze a table of star brightness and distance data and identify the pattern.

days.title: Unit 9 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 9 assessment on gravity and star brightness.

weeks.assessment: Unit 9 test; scale model reflection.

objectives: Measure and graph shadow length and direction
Relate shadow patterns to Earth's rotation

days.title: Shadow stick
days.work: Set up a shadow stick and mark and measure the shadow every hour from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.

days.title: Graphing shadows
days.work: Graph shadow length vs. time of day and describe the pattern.

days.title: Shadow direction
days.work: Use a compass to record the shadow direction for each hour and explain why it moves.

days.title: Globe model
days.work: Use a flashlight and globe to model day and night and shadows on a toothpick placed on California.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Build a simple sundial and write an explanation of how Earth's rotation causes shadow patterns.

weeks.assessment: Shadow graph and written explanation.

objectives: Graph day length data across the year
Explain patterns in daylight hours
materials: sunrise/sunset data table for your city

days.title: Daylight data
days.work: Collect sunrise and sunset times for the first day of each month and calculate hours of daylight.

days.title: Graphing day length
days.work: Graph daylight hours across the year and identify the longest and shortest days.

days.title: Tilt model
days.work: Use a lamp and tilted globe to model why California has longer days in summer.

days.title: Comparing cities
days.work: Compare day-length graphs for Los Angeles and Anchorage and describe the differences.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer data-analysis questions about day length patterns and take a quiz.

weeks.assessment: Day length graph and quiz.

objectives: Observe and record constellations
Explain why some stars are seen only in certain seasons
materials: star chart or free planetarium app

days.title: Night observation
days.work: Go outside after dark with a star chart and sketch 2 constellations and their positions.

days.title: Seasonal sky model
days.work: Walk around a lamp (sun) with constellation pictures on the walls to model why we see different stars each season.

days.title: Data table
days.work: Use a planetarium app to record which month Orion, Scorpius and the Big Dipper are visible at 9 p.m. and organize the data.

days.title: Second observation
days.work: Observe the sky again 2 hours later and record how constellations moved, explaining rotation.

days.title: Unit 10 assessment
days.work: Take the Unit 10 assessment on shadows, day length and seasonal stars.

weeks.assessment: Star observation sketches and Unit 10 test.

objectives: Ask a testable question
Plan and conduct a fair investigation

days.title: Choosing a question
days.work: Choose a testable question connected to this year's science (e.g., Does temperature affect how fast compost decomposes?).

days.title: Planning
days.work: Write a hypothesis, list variables and controls and write a step-by-step procedure.

days.title: Running trials
days.work: Conduct the investigation with at least 3 trials and record data.

days.title: More trials
days.work: Finish trials and organize data in a table.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a graph of the results and check it with a parent for accuracy.

weeks.assessment: Investigation plan and data table.

objectives: Analyze data and draw conclusions
Communicate findings in a science fair format

days.title: Analysis
days.work: Analyze data, describe patterns and decide whether the hypothesis was supported.

days.title: Conclusion
days.work: Write a conclusion with sources of error and a new question for further investigation.

days.title: Display
days.work: Create a science fair board or slideshow with question, hypothesis, procedure, data, graph and conclusion.

days.title: Science fair
days.work: Present the investigation to family or a co-op science fair and answer questions.

days.title: Year reflection
days.work: Review the science notebook and write about the three most important ideas learned this year.

weeks.assessment: Science fair rubric and year-end reflection.
